newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen spot slide fuels demand for vol.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen spot slide fuels demand for vol.

text.p: Dollar/yen options volatilities jumped off early lows in choppy Europe as battered spot veered to the downside again, traders said.
"Vols are just trading on the back of the spot movement -- people buy vol when the dollar goes down and sell when it goes up," said a senior options trader at a U.S. bank here.

One-month implied dollar/yen vol eased towards 11 percent in early Europe -- from late Thursday's levels of 12.2/12.6 -- as spot firmed, but were back up at 12.0/12.4 by 1022 GMT as spot took a new turn for the worse, traders reported.
Risk reversals spun more sharply in the yen's favour.
One-month dollar/yen risk reversals -- which gauge the market's preference for calls or puts -- were quoted at 1.2/1.6 percent for yen calls versus Thursday's level of 0.7/1.2.
In the spot market, dollar/yen opened at 116.73/83, up from yesterday's close of 116.20/25, after touching 117.00 overnight. But by European midsession it had lurched back to 115.43/53.

Divergent U.S./Japanese interest rate expectations and a barrage of yen-positive official comments have lately thrashed dollar/yen. Thursday's low of 114.70 yen marked a more than 12 yen decline since the beginning of May, when the dollar scaled a 55-month peak of 127.47.
Traders said activity was concentrated in the front end of the volatility curve, principally in the one-month, where sudden spot dollar/yen downspikes would trigger panic buying of vol.
"It won't take much of a move downward in the dollar to get a rise out of the front-end vols," said an options dealer at another U.S. house here.
Longer-dated vol was supported but slightly easier than late Thursday's levels.
Though more illiquid, mark/yen volatilities were also well underpinned as spot plummeted through 68.00 to a 20-month low of 67.81, dealers said.

One-month mark/yen vol was quoted at 10.1/10.6 percent versus late Thursday's 10.4/10.8. Dealers noted that risk reversals' skew for mark puts had become more pronounced, trading at 0.7/1.1 percent compared to 0.5 bid on Thursday.
Traders said the 67.30-50 yen zone was key, representing a 50 percent retracement of the mark's rally from its 58.70 low in April 1995 to the November 1996 high of 75.87.
"If we break 67.50 I think we'll go much better bid for mark puts," said another London-based options trader.
With the upwardly-mobile yen in the spotlight, dollar/mark volatilities were subdued, traders said.
One-month dollar/mark vol stood at 8.85/9.15 percent versus 8.9/9.2 late on Thursday, with risk reversals narrowly bid for mark calls at 0.1/0.2 percent -- little changed from yesterday.
